steps.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: original game production concept sheet, landscape, delicate graphite construction lines with controlled gouache color on warm off-white paper.
Primary request: draw the next spatial concept study for GUIHANG, the inhabited civilization mothership of Stellar Echoes. This is a local neighborhood cutaway, not a whole ship. Interpret a provisional 48-resident, TWO-DECK neighborhood. Make a beautiful, readable, inhabited spacecraft architecture study that can be reviewed beside an exact separate floor plan.
Input images: Image 1 is the existing habitation-lane sketch, for industrial materials and lived-in intimacy only. Image 2 is the cultivation-commons sketch, for consistent structure and cultivated-production character. Do not copy their layouts mechanically.
Composition: one large three-quarter longitudinal cutaway occupying most of the sheet, seen from slightly above one long side. A long, low, enclosed neighborhood slice with approximately 3:1 length-to-width proportion (working outer allocation 60m x20m). Only two occupied decks, no extra floors or city skyline. Roof and near side removed with clean heavy cut edges; far side and ends remain enclosed. Add just one small sectional detail at lower right showing an UPPER QUIET GALLERY enclosure. Do not fill the page with tiny plans or technical text.
Spatial organization, keep clear: a 4m-wide lower public street runs longitudinally between two banks of rooms. Lower left-near portion: intimate shared dining, six four-seat tables, warm composite tabletops, separate servery and tray-return recess, actual kitchen behind. Opposite is a communal room, then a glazed cultivation room with rack crops, hygiene vestibule and closed material transfer room. Laundry, everyday repair and neighborhood care are ordinary enclosed rooms farther along, not control centers. Rear service strips stay behind these lower rooms.
Upper deck: private cabin banks on BOTH long sides, a two-metre enclosed quiet gallery just inside each cabin bank, and a four-metre-wide central void open to the public street below. Crucially each upper gallery has a FULL-HEIGHT glazed acoustic wall facing the void, blue-gray frames with some opaque lower panels, not an open balcony railing. Cabin doors are closed; do not show all private beds to the public street. Two end cores each contain stairs and an enclosed lift reserve linking exactly the two decks. Do not add a third circulation level. Upper enclosed gallery and lower active street should be visually different.
Habitation: ordinary residents of different ages and jobs at human scale, subtle actions including a returned shift worker carrying lunch, a parent beside a child, someone carrying clean folded linen, two residents chatting away from circulation. Do not depict 48 identical figures or 48 people crowded in one room. Architecture is inhabited but uncluttered, restrained and dignified, not a shopping mall or luxury cruise ship.
Materials: warm ivory removable panels, blue-gray structural ribs, graphite service recesses, small brick-red identification accents, warm amber work lamps; crops provide limited natural green, textiles and personal threshold objects provide warmth. Clear construction thickness, functional industrial science-fiction beauty; original design, no franchise logos or copied iconic shapes.
Text (verbatim): only "GUIHANG", "NEIGHBORHOOD / N48", "SPATIAL STUDY", and in the small detail "QUIET GALLERY". No other text, no invented numeric dimensions or pseudo-technical labels.
Local flat unrolled concept only: no star windows, no magic gravity generators, no rotational axle interface, no spaceship exterior around it, no unproven ring radius. All inhabitants share the same local down direction. This drawing is a concept interpretation; prioritize legible relationships and believable scale, not claims of a CAD projection.

Use case: precise-object-edit.
Edit ONLY the upper QUIET GALLERY enclosure in the supplied GUIHANG neighborhood cutaway. Keep the paper, title, overall composition, TWO occupied decks, long inhabited spacecraft slice, lower dining room, cultivation glazing, people, materials, lighting, both end stairs, and the lower-right quiet-gallery inset unchanged.
Concrete defect: in the large main cutaway the upper corridor has only a waist-high glass guard; the upper half is open to the noisy lower street. Its inset correctly shows a floor-to-ceiling glazed wall. Correct the MAIN view so that it also has the same complete acoustic glazing.
Preserve the existing blue-gray lower sill/guard frames, and extend EVERY main upper-corridor glazing bay upward to the overhead structural beam, with thin blue-gray mullions and transparent panes from the upper-deck floor to the ceiling. Draw subtle visible glass reflections in the upper panes, a continuous sealed head rail under the roof beam, and sparse restrained metal panel strips so the complete enclosure is unmistakable. No open gaps above the old railing. Keep people and closed private doors visible THROUGH the glass, not on the public side of it.
At each end of this upper glazed corridor place one closed full-height framed access door between the quiet corridor and the stair landing, as part of the same enclosure. Leave the stair flights outside that closed quiet-gallery envelope.
Do not add a floor, extra roof, new rooms, dimensions, labels, icons, or windows looking into outer space. Do not change the small lower-right inset, which already has the intended full-height glazing. Do not redesign the ground-floor architecture. Preserve the original sketch style and all other elements.

Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: original game architectural detail concept, landscape, hand-drawn graphite and controlled gouache on warm off-white sketchbook paper.
Primary request: GUIHANG cultivation hygiene threshold, the focused follow-up to the previous cultivation-commons image. Resolve the misleading half-height public doorway in that older detail. This is a NEW consistent architectural study, not an edit of the whole old scene.
Input image 1: existing cultivation commons sketch, visual-language reference and context only. Retain its warm ivory panels, blue-gray structure, graphite trim, restrained brick-red room coding, amber lamps and practical cultivated racks. Do not replicate the half-height doorway from its lower-left detail.
Composition: a single large three-quarter cutaway of a compact rectangular 4m-wide by6m-deep hygiene vestibule, shown from the public/front side and slightly above. Roof and front-right wall are selectively removed; put visible graphite cut-edge hatching on removed walls. Crucially retain the COMPLETE front public-door assembly, including both jambs, overhead lintel, and full-height door leaf (approximately 1.2m wide by2.2m tall), even where the neighboring wall is cut away. It should be visibly taller than the standing adult. A second complete door is on the LEFT side wall farther back, opening toward the cultivation room. These two doorways form an L-shaped human route. They are NOT opposite one another. Show both door leaves closed with readable seals, not a route drawn through an open hole.
Interior arrangement: a compact wash basin fixed on the REAR wall, changing bench and clean-clothing cabinet against the RIGHT wall, an unblocked central standing/turning area. One staff member inside in ordinary coveralls, changing into a clean oversmock; hands anatomically simple and natural. One resident is outside on the public side looking toward the production window, no resident inside crops. No airlock machinery, no pressure meters claiming a space lock, no oversized decontamination chamber.
The cultivation room is only glimpsed beyond the LEFT wall's adjacent observation glazing, with a rack and worker. A tiny companion lower-right diagrammatic vignette shows the full public door front elevation beside a human silhouette, clearly a full door taller than the adult, not a waist-high gate. Do not add new corridor directions or contradictory door positions in that vignette.
Do NOT put a cargo pass-through in the human doorway: harvested material and waste are handled on a different rear service edge outside this personnel vignette. Show no supply cart parked in the doorway. The full-height glazed partition between public walkway and growing room is continuous.
Text (verbatim): "GUIHANG", "CULTIVATION THRESHOLD", "PUBLIC", "GROW", "FULL DOOR FRAME". Use PUBLIC at the front side and GROW at left. No other annotations, no fictitious engineering dimensions or dense UI.
Original polished science-fiction concept craft, detailed yet readable, comfortable functional home inside a machine. Stable local gravity, no outer-space windows, no magical technology, no photorealistic product render, no franchise insignia.
